---
title: Generic Backups
---

The `generic` subcommand runs standard restic operations against any configured
backup. Backup sources may be files or directories anywhere on the machine.

Set `RESTIC_BACKUPS_CONFIG` first, or pass `--config` before `generic`. See the
[Quick Start](quick-start.qmd) for a complete first backup.

## Commands

| Group | Command | Purpose | Remote storage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Repository | `generic repository list` | Show configured repositories | No |
| Repository | `generic repository init` | Initialize each new enabled repository | Yes |
| Repository | `generic repository prime-cache [REPOSITORY]` | Cache and validate repository metadata | Yes |
| Repository | `generic repository destroy [REPOSITORY]` | Permanently erase one repository | Yes |
| Backup | `generic backup list` | Show configured backup jobs | No |
| Backup | `generic backup run [BACKUP]` | Create a snapshot from configured paths | Yes |
| Backup | `generic backup data-dir [BACKUP]` | Print the managed private-data directory | No |
| Snapshot | `generic snapshot list [BACKUP]` | List snapshots for a configured backup | Yes |
| Snapshot | `generic snapshot forget [BACKUP]` | Forget one tagged snapshot and prune | Yes |
| Restic | `generic restic run --backup ID ...` | Pass trailing arguments directly to restic | Depends on restic command |

Commands that accept `[BACKUP]` prompt when it is omitted in an interactive
terminal. Non-interactive callers must provide the backup ID.

Running `restic-backups generic` without a subcommand in an interactive terminal
opens a section menu for repositories, backups, snapshots, and advanced restic
commands. Explicit subcommands remain available for scripts and scheduled jobs.
**Advanced restic** reads the installed restic version's command list and
descriptions, lets you select one, then prompts only for its arguments. Enter
`--help` at that prompt to see the selected command's options.

`generic repository list` shows every store, even when no configured backup
references it. `generic backup list` shows the configured backup jobs.

`generic repository init` reports each configured store, skips disabled or
already initialized stores, and initializes every enabled store that is missing.

`generic repository prime-cache` runs `restic check --with-cache` for one
repository. It downloads repository indexes, snapshots, and tree metadata into
the configured cache while also validating repository structure. It does not
download backed-up file contents; restic only does that when `--read-data` is
requested explicitly.

## Create a snapshot

Configure the local source paths once, then select the backup by its ID:

```yaml
backups:
  - id: documents
    restic-store-id: personal-store
    paths:
      - ~/Documents
      - ~/Desktop
```

```sh
uv run restic-backups generic backup run documents
```

The command expands `~`, passes the paths to `restic backup`, and applies the
backup ID as the restic tag unless `tag` is explicitly configured. Every run
creates a snapshot of the complete source state while restic uploads only new
or changed file data.

## List snapshots

List snapshots with the configured backup tag:

```sh
uv run restic-backups generic snapshot list documents
```

The table shows each snapshot's short restic ID, timestamp, host, paths, and tags.

## Forget one snapshot

```sh
uv run restic-backups generic snapshot forget
```

Forgetting is interactive-only. Select a configured backup, select one snapshot
with its configured restic tag, and confirm. The CLI runs
`restic forget --prune`, so the snapshot and data no longer referenced by any
other snapshot are permanently removed. The configured backup and repository
remain available.

When several configured backups share a repository, their restic tags keep their
snapshots distinct in the picker.

## Permanently destroy a repository

```sh
uv run restic-backups generic repository destroy
```

Destruction is interactive-only. The CLI shows the full S3 target, asks for a
yes/no confirmation, then requires the exact repository ID. It deletes every
object, object version, and delete marker below the configured `bucket` and
`key_prefix`. It does not delete the bucket or change the YAML configuration.

The provider credentials need permission to list objects and versions and to
delete objects and versions. An empty `key_prefix` is always rejected to prevent
accidental bucket deletion.

::: {.callout-danger}
Repository deletion is irreversible. Snapshots, indexes, repository keys, and
encrypted data are all erased. The configured restic password cannot recover
them.
:::

## Common operations

```sh
# Inspect and check the repository
uv run restic-backups generic snapshot list documents
uv run restic-backups generic restic run --backup documents check

# Restore a snapshot
uv run restic-backups generic restic run --backup documents \
  restore <snapshot-id> --target /tmp/documents-restore
```

Arguments after the backup selection are passed to restic unchanged. The CLI
exports the selected repository and credentials only to the child process and
does not print them. For the `backup` command, it also adds the configured restic
tag automatically; additional `--tag` arguments remain supported.

## Managed data directory

```sh
uv run restic-backups generic backup data-dir documents
```

The result follows
`data/<store-id>/<bucket>/<key-prefix>/<backup-id>/` beside the selected config
file. It is for private generated metadata; generic backup sources do not need
to live there.

## Cold S3 storage

`GLACIER_IR` supports immediate access. `GLACIER` and `DEEP_ARCHIVE` permit
uploads, but retrieval-related commands require the configured restore policy
and an explicit acknowledgement:

```sh
ALLOW_ARCHIVE_RETRIEVAL=1 uv run restic-backups generic restic run \
  --backup archive restore latest --target /tmp/archive-restore
```

Other restic commands are rejected for cold repositories when the CLI cannot
determine that they are safe. See [Configuration](configuration.qmd) for the
archive policy fields.
